https://www.politico.eu/article/andy-bur.text: LONDON — Prime Minister Andy Burnham will lead a meeting of the government's emergency committee Wednesday afternoon in response to ongoing heatwaves, droughts and wildfires across the U.K. COBR (Cabinet Office Briefing Room) meetings are convened during a crisis or emergency — and come as the record-breaking conditions take a severe toll on U.K. infrastructure. The crisis is an early test for Burnham, who came to office just last month. Advertisement Advertisement A Downing Street spokesperson said: “We know how challenging this summer is proving, particularly for firefighters tackling wildfires, farmers working in drought conditions, and NHS staff in busy A&E units. “We will continue to take the action needed to keep communities safe, protect water supplies, support farming communities and safeguard the environment.” Britons are this week bracing for their fifth heatwave of 2026, with some temperatures forecast to exceed 36C. The Met Office, Britain's national weather service, has warned that this summer is set to be the U.K.'s hottest since records began. More than two-thirds of England is now in drought after the driest July since records began in 1836. The whole of Wales is also in drought, and more than 27 million people across the U.K. are facing water restrictions including hosepipe bans. The U.K. is grappling with wildfires including at the New Forest national park in south England. The National Fire Chiefs Council responded to 458 wildfires last month, its busiest month on record. 'Snail's pace' The rival Green Party first demanded a COBR meeting weeks ago after a wildfire engulfed parts of Suffolk in eastern England. Green Leader Zack Polanski said Wednesday's meeting is “only a first step. This is a climate emergency which is leading to hundreds of deaths and stretching our firefighters, health staff and farmers to the limit. What we urgently need is concrete action.” Advertisement Advertisement Liberal Democrat Energy Spokesperson Pippa Heylings warned a COBR meeting alone “will not put out fires or protect our communities,” and said government is “moving at a snail’s pace.” Prior to today's COBR, the U.K.'s National Drought Group and Severe Weather Resilience Network have held regular meetings, and the government has also vowed to work with water companies to build nine new reservoirs for the U.K. — which built its last reservoir back in 1992. U.K. climate advisers have meanwhile spent much of the summer urging the country to up its game when it comes to adaptation for a warming world. The Committee on Climate Change, a government advisory body, said in May that cooling to protect from heat, “increased flood preparedness, and improved water management are the highest priorities.” “Deploying these adaptations at scale will help avoid loss of life – particularly amongst those most vulnerable to climate impacts – and unnecessary damage and disruption to people and to the economy,” it said. The U.K. has been “built to a climate that no longer exists,” Swenja Surminski, a member of the Climate Change Committee Adaptation Committee, told MPs in June. Additional reporting by Charlie Cooper. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-new.text: Lt Gen Charles Costanza, a senior US Army commander overseeing military operations in Europe, has been abruptly removed from his post, the Army confirmed Friday. The decision came nearly two months before he was expected to hand over command, while the circumstances behind his removal remain unclear.Costanza commanded the Army’s V Corps, a key formation responsible for overseeing US Army forces and coordinating operations across Europe.Who is Charles Costanza?Costanza is an armor officer who has led V Corps since April 2024. Before taking command of the corps, he served as commander of the 3rd Infantry Division at Fort Stewart, Georgia.V Corps has become particularly significant since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Partially based in Poland, the corps helps coordinate US support for Ukraine and manages the American military presence along NATO’s eastern flank. The Army said Costanza was removed from command in recent days. Brig Gen John B Mountford, V Corps’ deputy commanding general for readiness, is currently serving as acting commanding general.Also Read: US has nearly exhausted key long-range precision missiles in Trump's Iran offensive: ReportWhy was Charles Costanza removed?The Army has not publicly disclosed the reason for Costanza’s removal.His departure comes amid a wider shake-up of senior US military leadership under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. More than two dozen high-ranking officers have been removed or sidelined during Hegseth’s tenure, often without detailed public explanations.However, a source familiar with Costanza’s removal told ABC News that his case was unrelated to Hegseth’s broader effort to reshape the military’s senior leadership and was not driven by political considerations.No further explanation was provided about what prompted Costanza’s early departure.Who will replace Charles Costanza?Maj Gen Thomas Feltey had already been Senate-confirmed to take over the V Corps command in October. Costanza’s removal therefore brings forward a leadership transition that had already been planned.The Army has not indicated whether Feltey will now assume the position earlier than scheduled.Also Read: 'Mediators compromised': US expert's big allegation against Pakistan, Qatar as Trump hints at talks with IranWhy is V Corps important?Costanza’s removal comes as the US military continues to adjust its presence in Europe.The Pentagon downsized the US military footprint in Europe this year, including abruptly cancelling a planned deployment of the Army’s 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division, from Fort Hood, Texas, to Poland.The decision drew criticism in Warsaw. President Donald Trump later announced that the US would position 5,000 troops in Poland.With V Corps playing a central role in coordinating US Army activities in Europe and along NATO’s eastern flank, the sudden removal of its commander has drawn attention.For now, however, the Army has not publicly explained why Costanza was removed nearly two months before his expected change of command.

https://allafrica.com/stories/2026081404.text: Angolan Diplomats At New Hungarian President Election Event Luanda — Members of the Diplomatic Mission of Angola to Hungary witnessed on Tuesday (11), in Budapest, the election of the new Hungarian President, András Baka, during a Solemn Session of Parliament dedicated to the subject. According to a note from the Angolan diplomatic mission in that country, the Embassy of Angola in Hungary, like the diplomatic corps in general, is of the opinion that the election of András Baka could open a new politico-institutional stage in the country, particularly within the framework of ongoing constitutional reforms and the government's intention to strengthen the country's relations with European institutions, as well as with the rest of the world. The President of Hungary is elected through an indirect system of voting, that is through the National Assembly (Parliament) which has 199 MPs. The new Head of State, András Baka, was elected with 146 votes in favour, zero votes against and zero abstentions, as the opposition opted for an empty-chair (absence) policy. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Despite this fact, the President-elect surpassed the constitutional two-thirds majority required for election in the first round. He is scheduled to take office on August 19, 2026. The election took place following the early termination of the mandate of the previous President of the Republic, Tamás Sulyok, effective from July 20, 2026, following the amendments introduced by the 17th Amendment to the Fundamental Law of Hungary. András Baka, former President of the Supreme Court of Hungary and former Judge at the European Court of Human Rights, was put forward as a candidate by TISZA, the party supporting the Government of Prime Minister Péter Magyar, which currently holds a majority of over two thirds in the National Assembly.
